prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010: Change That Works for You — Building a Fairer Britain

Core vision: hard‑wiring fairness into national life by redistributing economic, social, political and financial power. Four priorities:
- Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- A fair chance for every child
- A fair future with green jobs and sustainable growth
- A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring liberties

Fair taxes and responsible finances
- Raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000, worth ~£700 to most basic‑rate taxpayers; 3.6m lowest earners/pensioners off income tax.
- Funded by: aligning capital gains with income tax; restricting pension tax relief to basic rate; a 1% “mansion tax” on property value over £2m; anti‑avoidance; replacing Air Passenger Duty with per‑plane duty (higher for some domestic flights).
- Banking levy until retail/investment banking are separated; break up big banks; curb bonus incentives.
- Identified savings >£15bn (e.g., scrap ID cards and biometric passports, reform prisons with presumption against short sentences, cancel Eurofighter tranche 3B, scale back quangos/inspection, cap public sector pay rises at £400 for two years, restrict tax credits, end Child Trust Fund payments).
- Establish a cross‑party Council on Financial Stability; aim to halve the deficit by 2013–14; protect frontline health services.

Jobs, growth and green transition
- One‑year green stimulus creating ~100,000 jobs: shipyard conversion for offshore wind, eco cash‑back for home efficiency/micro‑generation, public‑building insulation, bus scrappage, bringing 250,000 empty homes into use.
- Create a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for transport/energy; support local enterprise funds and regional stock exchanges.
- Targeted deregulation, fairer business rates, superfast broadband roll‑out; support mutuals/co‑ops; reform takeover rules.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one support for disadvantaged pupils; stronger SEN assessment/support; improved teacher training.
- Independent Educational Standards Authority; slimmed‑down curriculum; scaled‑back SATs at 11; a General Diploma blending academic/vocational routes; more 14–19 college options.
- Phase out university tuition fees over six years; new national bursary scheme; expand apprenticeships and foundation degrees.

Health and care
- Reinvest savings from bureaucracy into cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia and prevention; halve Department of Health bureaucracy; abolish Strategic Health Authorities.
- Integrate health and social care; elected Local Health Boards; patient entitlements for timely diagnosis/treatment; expand talking therapies; prioritise dementia research; responsible alcohol measures.
- Immediate restoration of the earnings link for the basic state pension (triple lock principle) and carers’ respite; scrap compulsory retirement ages.

Communities, crime, housing and transport
- 3,000 more police, less bureaucracy, elected police authorities, restorative justice; make prisoners work and contribute to victim funds.
- Firm but fair immigration: reintroduce exit checks; National Border Force; regional points‑based system; earned route to citizenship for long‑standing, law‑abiding residents; independent asylum agency; end child detention; allow asylum seekers to work.
- Housing: insulate homes; energy‑efficient new builds; revive empty homes; enable council housebuilding.
- Transport: invest in rail (including high speed) via Infrastructure Bank; cut regulated rail fares in real terms; stronger passenger rights; empower councils on buses; safer cycling/walking.

Environment and climate
- Zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; ≥40% electricity from non‑carbon sources by 2020 (with emphasis on marine/offshore); improve grid and develop a European Supergrid.
- Block new unabated coal; oppose new nuclear as costly vs. efficiency/renewables; tighten commercial/public energy efficiency.
- Replace APD with per‑plane duty; cancel Heathrow third runway; higher duty on some domestic flights; rural fuel discount.
- “Zero waste” strategy; stronger biodiversity targets; more access to countryside.

Politics and civil liberties
- Fair votes (STV), reduce MPs by ~150, fixed‑term parliaments, fully elected smaller second chamber, written constitution via citizens’ convention.
- Recall corrupt MPs; cap donations at £10,000; lobbyist register; extend FOI; require all MPs/candidates to be UK tax‑resident/domiciled.
- Freedom Bill: regulate CCTV; curb surveillance/databases; restore jury trial/protest rights; reform libel law; reduce pre‑charge detention to 14 days; allow intercept evidence; scrap control orders; clean up DNA database.

Foreign, defence and development
- Lead on EU‑backed climate action; financial regulation; pro‑EU reform; future in/out referendum only with fundamental treaty change; euro entry only if conditions and referendum support.
- Meet 0.7% GNI aid by 2013; new development finance; anti‑corruption and tax haven measures.
- Strategic defence review; no like‑for‑like Trident replacement; pay rise for lower ranks; modernise service family housing; tighter arms export controls; judicial inquiry into torture/ rendition; pursue two‑state solution in Middle East; conditions‑based Afghanistan strategy enabling troop drawdown in next Parliament.
